punchline: By many measures life has never been safer or more prosperous, yet many people feel more hopeless; Mark Manson calls it the paradox of progress.
thirty_sec: Mark Manson points out something odd: by many measures life has never been safer or richer, yet lots of people feel more anxious and hopeless. Part of his explanation is hope itself. To hope, you have to feel something is missing now. Aim all your hope at the future and the present starts to feel never good enough. His blunt answer: don't hope for better, just be better.
question: What's a 'once this happens, I'll be happy' that you've been holding onto for a while?
